pr_title: Fix `DirectorySelector` causing a stack overflow when trying to open an inaccessible directory
pr_body:
Fixes #13602 

Attempting to open a nonexistent folder will open the next existing parent directory instead.
pr_comments:
The original folder no longer existing is only one case of the issue this is attempting to fix. Consider the following scenario (for brevity, I'll use unix commands to describe it):

1. First, create a two-level deep directory structure:
```
~$ mkdir test && cd test
~/test$ mkdir test2
```
2. Navigate to `~/test/test2` in a picker in the game.
3. Now execute the following:
```
~/test$ chmod -x test2 && cd ..
~$ chmod -x test
```
4. Go back to the game and try to navigate one level up, to `~/test`. The game will crash.

What I did there is I revoked traversal permissions to both the new directory and the original, and triggered this issue all the same - the directories still exist, they are just no longer traversable. And that crash's all due to the recursive `CurrentPath.Value` set in the `catch` branch which does no checks whatsoever as to whether going back to the directory is even permitted.

To eliminate this for good, `updateDisplay` must not change `CurrentPath.Value` again. Or, at least if it does try to restore it to the old directory, it should first check before leaping and bail to a known safe location if it fails (filesystem root?)

Also a bit of an aside, but this component was since moved to the framework, but we are still maintaining a copy here. I think we're going to hit the same issue there.. so we'll want to apply the same fix and (hopefully) move this local component over to using the framework implementation. Maybe as part of this change, maybe as a follow-up.

Let's make sure to at least open an issue tracking this before this issue is resolved.
I've pushed in a round of changes that in my opinion bring this to a mergeable state. They ended up being pretty much a rewrite, however, so I am not merging without a second check.

Sure, I can do that as a follow up (as well as migrate the game to use the framework component). Maybe it would even be best to port this framework-side immediately and supersede this PR with another one tearing out the duplicated implementation?

Good point on the comment, I'll fix it up as well.
You'll probably find the changes are quite easy to port over either way. I don't mind merging this one and doing the combination as a follow up, up to you since you're the one working on it.

I have changes queued to replace the game-side directory/file selectors with the framework component, just couldn't get them 100% ready in time today (and I don't want to spam PRs, either).

Going to block this pending that; the framework-side port is PR'd, and the game-side pull that will tear out the local game copy will supersede this pull.

issue_context.title: File browser silently crashes when navigating back into a folder that has been deleted/moved
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug:** 
repro steps:
1. create a temporary folder (iny my case ``test1``)
2. create another folder inside ``test1`` (in my case ``test2``)
3. open the file browser in osu and navigate into ``test2``
4. delete the ``test1`` folder
5. try to access ``test1`` inside osu

**Screenshots or videos showing encountered issue:** 

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/43358824/122782146-c4a29b00-d2b0-11eb-8663-2cc9d8a0285d.mp4


**osu!lazer version:** 
2021.619.1

**Logs:**
[database.log](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/6687482/database.log)
[network.log](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/6687483/network.log)
[performance.log](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/6687484/performance.log)
[performance-draw.log](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/6687485/performance-draw.log)
[performance-update.log](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/6687486/performance-update.log)
[runtime.log](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/6687487/runtime.log)
[updater.log](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/6687488/updater.log)

osu! lazer doesn't seem to generate any crash logs but im still gonna upload them just in case.
comments: The fact that this doesn't generate a crash log is the most disturbing part. Marking as highest priority until we at least figure out why that's the case.

A quick debug session with VS shows the game crashing with exit code `0x800703e9` which is a stack overflow error, causing the runtime to abort, hence why nothing gets logged. The error originates from there:

https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/3f336d88ec651fc7fb0b5bb9c99a96c944366e98/osu.Game/Graphics/UserInterfaceV2/DirectorySelector.cs#L80-L105

The selector upon catching a `DirectoryNotFound` exception while trying to navigate to the newly selected directory path (which doesn't exist anymore) will set back the current directory path to the previous one, which also doesn't exist anymore and this will recurse infinitely since both the old and the new directory paths don't exist.

review_comments: Is `directoryChanging` not going to get stuck in an incorrect state here? Wondering if we want to use `try-finally` with the `directoryChanging = false;` inside the `finally` block here.
